items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And we had Joe Johnson on guitar.

ctx.x: See Roy Palmer was first a guitar player where we had a little three piece band, see. Then we converted Roy to trumpet player, see. And we had Joe Johnson on guitar. My brother had an E flat trumpet and trumpet players used to use an E flat trumpet around and brass bands. So Joe kept a fool with his E flat trumpet and learned how to play trumpet. And he had a guy that called the trumpet player, Ovit, Ovit Jackson, that's really Ovit, you know that's French, you know that. See he didn't make it on trumpet, so Roy…
And Joe Johnson, the trumpet player, had been playing guitar?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: And Joe Johnson was our guitar player.

ctx.x: It was around 1997 and 1999 when my brother bought that big bass for me. Uh-huh. He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, yes. Roy Palmer was our guitar player. You had to see what became a trombone player? No, let me see what Roy was playing. Roy was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And Joe Johnson was our guitar player. So Joe Johnson learned trumpet and Roy Palmer and Roy Palmer was good too. Joe died. That's what I tell the guys, they read about…
Sure. Why would you play? Bass drum?
